candidates.subject: roseate spoonbill
candidates.title: After preening
candidates.body:
Worked a loose feather out of my breast. It drifted away so slowly I thought I could catch it.

Missed. Tried again.

Now I'm leaning off the branch with my bill open, waiting for the thing I just pulled out to come back.
candidates.visibleScene: Clear immature spoonbill leaning over a log, open bill above a small loose white feather; pale breast feathers are fluffed and one foot grips the log. Candidate.
candidates.fictionBoundary: The white feather below the open bill, fluffed breast and inclined head are visible. Preening the feather free, its origin on her breast, drifting motion, failed snaps, and change from removing it to wanting it back are fiction. No source description claims these temporal details. The image supplies the exact object and relationship rather than an unrelated species portrait.
candidates.chronology: Use as an early immature scene, before adult Lark events. Fully feathered head and pale pink plumage indicate immature age by Cornell comparison; no exact numerical age or subspecies assigned. Do not append after adult scenes as if she regrew juvenile head plumage.

evaluatedDrafts.body: Cleaned my breast until no feather sat crooked. Took my bill away. A little white one followed. Snapped at it. Missed. Snapped again. It drifted down to the water. I leaned after it with half my breast sticking out.
evaluatedDrafts.reason: Complicates the turn with perfect grooming and extra disarray; final version stays with her changing desire for the same feather.

evaluatedDrafts.body: Stopped digging when the earth rustled behind me. Turned. Nothing. Put my claws back in. Something moved again. I kept looking over my shoulder until a little slope of the dirt I had thrown out slid against my rump.
evaluatedDrafts.reason: A complete causal draft, but the sharp portrait does not show sliding dirt, turned digging posture or a substantial mound. Too much of its specific incident is offscreen, and the self-caused alarm is familiar.

evaluatedDrafts.body: Sat up to see over the grass. The smell was stronger down below. Lowered my head. Lost the view. Sat up again. Stayed there with my nose lifted, waiting for the ground to tell me from farther away.
evaluatedDrafts.reason: Actual pose fits, but sensory inconvenience does not become a sufficiently particular consequence. No recommendation for integration.

biology.supports: Pale pink immature birds retain a feathered head; characteristic spoon bill; roosting near wetlands. No exact age used.
Birds maintain feathers by preening with the bill. Does not document removal or attempted recapture in this photograph.
